author: somnergy
content:
I don't agree with the lack of tick against "The team maintaining the guest program must be considered sustainable". Erigontech (and associated people) have been maintaining Erigon and other core Ethereum software and EIPs for like 7 years now. I would consider that sufficient for this criterion. We are also confident in our sub-team within Erigontech to maintain Zilkworm for a long time.

**Regarding forks and tests support**

We wish to disburse support for standard formats and tests through our own repositories and not contribute to forks actively. However, we welcome forks and experiments. We support standard EESTs for a very long time in all supported architectures and zkVMs, more work on the way. For new formats, we will introduce support on a rolling basis as also informed earlier to <@774033563732541451> 

Zilkworm is stateless so, "zilkworm-stateless" is redundant. But it is still welcome as an experiment.

ELF files and artifacts will be published in future in more places too. Currently it's already in https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases

We are in no hurry to be tagged compliant or be published w.r.t zilkworm. We are focusing on quality, innovation and efficiency. We will make releases as soon as possible for the latest things.

**Regarding Licensing**

We may reconsider the MIT licensing in future, but for now we will stick to Apache 2.0 on Zilkworm and associated repos. We are unable to commit on this in either direction internally or externally because of market uncertainty.

Further, code like this is extremely vulnerable to bugs and exploits, so it is not recommended to park its future on untested hands and hope for the best. For that reason we are unable to endorse or evaluate third parties for this either.
